difficultyRationale: The transient/managed/detached state model is foundational to JPA but rarely tested precisely — most candidates can name the states without knowing which operations actually move an entity between them.
prompt: A transactional method does: `Order o = new Order();` then `em.persist(o);` then, inside the same transaction, modifies `o.setStatus("SHIPPED")` without calling any further `EntityManager` method, and the transaction commits. At which point does `o` become a *managed* entity, and what happens to the status change made after `persist()`?
explanation: `new Order()` creates a *transient* entity, known to no persistence context. Calling `em.persist(o)` makes it *managed*: the entity is now tracked by the persistence context and scheduled for insertion. Because it stays managed for the rest of the transaction, any field mutation on it afterward (`setStatus(...)`) is picked up automatically by dirty checking at flush/commit time — no further `save()` or `merge()` call is needed for that change to be written.

options.text: `o` becomes managed only when the transaction commits, not when `persist()` is called; the status change made right after `persist()` is therefore made to a still-transient object and is silently lost unless `merge()` is called before commit.
options.explanation: `persist()` itself is what transitions the entity to managed, immediately, within the call — not the later commit. The status change is made to an already-managed entity and is not lost.

options.text: `o` becomes managed when `persist()` is called, but field mutations made after that point are only picked up if the entity is explicitly re-attached with `em.merge(o)` before the transaction commits, since `persist()` only takes a snapshot at call time.
options.explanation: There is no snapshot-at-call-time limitation and no need to call `merge()` on an already-managed entity; `merge()` is for re-attaching a *detached* entity, which `o` never becomes here. Dirty checking tracks ongoing changes automatically.

options.text: `o` becomes managed the moment `em.persist(o)` returns; the later status change is applied to that managed entity and is automatically detected by dirty checking and written out at flush/commit time, with no extra save call required.
options.explanation: Correct. `persist()` is exactly the operation that moves an entity from transient to managed. Once managed, in-memory field changes are tracked by the persistence context's dirty checking and flushed automatically.

options.text: `persist()` only reserves a database identifier for `o` without changing its lifecycle state; `o` remains transient until the surrounding transaction commits, at which point it transitions directly from transient to detached.
options.explanation: `persist()` changes the entity's lifecycle state immediately, to managed, not merely reserving an identifier. There is also no direct transient-to-detached transition; an entity becomes detached only after being managed first (typically when its persistence context closes).

references.title: Jakarta Persistence Specification 3.1 — §3.2.2 Persisting an Entity Instance (persist() makes an entity managed; §3.2.4 synchronization at flush/commit)
